6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e148.description: Turkish minced-lamb kebabs seasoned with red pepper paste and pul biber, chilled, shaped onto skewers and grilled.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0c8.description: Light Scandinavian pancake puffs flavoured with cardamom, turned in a special pan and served with powdered sugar and jam.
instructions: Whisk the flour, salt, sugar, baking powder and cardamom together in a large bowl.
Separate the eggs and add the yolks to the flour mixture. Pour in the buttermilk and whisk until smooth. Cover and refrigerate for about 30 minutes.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, then carefully fold them into the batter.
Heat the æbleskiver pan over a medium heat. Once hot, brush each hole with butter and fill almost to the top with batter.
Once the edges are firm, use a knitting needle or wooden skewer to turn each æbleskive a quarter turn. Keep turning until they form golden-brown spheres.
Remove from the pan and serve with powdered sugar and jam.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e141.description: Potatoes crisped in the air fryer and served under a smoky paprika and tomato sauce.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0de.description: Argentine shortbread sandwich cookies filled with dulce de leche and rolled in coconut.
instructions: Make the dough: cream the butter and sugar. Add the egg yolks and lemon zest, then gradually mix in the flour and cornstarch to form a dough. Chill for 1 hour; chilled dough rolls more easily and spreads less in the oven.
Bake the cookies: roll out the dough, cut into circles and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 12–15 minutes. Let cool.
Assemble: spread dulce de leche on one cookie and sandwich it with another. Roll the edges in coconut.
If you like, dip the alfajores in melted chocolate and let them set on a wire rack.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e103.description: Steamed carrots finished in garlic, olive oil, cumin and cinnamon, with a squeeze of lemon.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0bd.description: A simple one-pan apple cake made with a sour-milk batter and a sugar and cinnamon top.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and butter a baking pan.
Peel and core the apples and cut them into slices.
Beat the eggs and sugar together until light and foamy.
Mix together the flour, salt and bicarbonate of soda.
Add the dry ingredients to the egg mixture, then stir in the sour milk a little at a time.
Pour the batter into the pan and press the apple slices into the top. Sprinkle over a little sugar and cinnamon and bake for 30 minutes.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0af.description: Plain corn-flour arepas, browned in a skillet and finished in the oven until they sound hollow.
instructions: Put the corn flour in a bowl and add the salted water little by little, mixing until all the water is used and the flour has become a dough. For more flavour, use chicken or beef broth in place of the water. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Shape the dough into rounds about 3 inches across and ½ inch thick. Cook them slowly in a lightly greased skillet until a crust forms on each side.
Transfer to a baking dish and bake at 350°F for about 20 minutes, until the arepas sound hollow when tapped.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e16c.description: Venezuelan corn arepas split and stuffed with slow-cooked shredded beef and grated cheese.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e10b.description: Dutch puff-pastry biscuits rolled in cinnamon, cardamom and lime sugar and baked until caramelised.
instructions: Defrost the puff pastry.
Flour the work surface. Stack the pastry sheets on top of each other and roll them out until the stack is as thin as a single sheet.
Cut out rounds or ovals with a cutter, as close together as you can to get as many biscuits as possible.
Mix the vanilla sugar with the cinnamon, cardamom and lime zest in a small bowl.
Clear the flour from the counter and sprinkle it with a little of the sugar mix.
Brush the pastry shapes with egg, dip them in the sugar mix and roll them gently to press the sugar in.
Lay them on a lined baking sheet and leave to rest for 20–25 minutes; this makes them crisper. Heat the oven to 180°C meanwhile.
Bake for about 25 minutes, until golden brown and the sugar has caramelised.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e15c.description: Argentine mixed grill: salted beef cuts, chorizo and morcilla cooked slowly over wood coals.
instructions: Prepare the fire: start a fire of wood and charcoal in your grill and let it burn down to coals. Wood adds flavour; charcoal holds the temperature.
Season the meat: generously salt the beef cuts just before they go on the grill.
Grill the meat: place the beef on the grill with the thickest cuts farthest from the coals. Add the chorizo and morcilla once the beef has been cooking for a while.
Cook the meat, turning occasionally, until it reaches the doneness you like. Ribs can take up to 2 hours; thinner cuts cook faster.
Rest the meat for about 10 minutes before slicing. Serve with chimichurri, a fresh tomato salad and crusty bread.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e167.description: Grilled aubergine slices spread with hummus, crumbed and grilled again, with a walnut, parsley and tomato salad.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e101.description: A wheel of brie spread with spiced sorrel jam, wrapped in puff pastry and baked.
instructions: Make the jam: combine the dried sorrel, brown sugar, ginger, cinnamon, vanilla pod and orange zest with the boiled water in a medium pot.

Bring to the boil and cook until the sorrel petals soften, then reduce the heat and simmer until thickened, adding a splash of water if it catches. Let it cool before using. The jam can be made a day ahead.
Slice the brie in half horizontally, or leave the wheel whole and trim off the top rind.
Spread a generous layer of jam on the top of the wheel, or on one cut half and sandwich the halves back together.
Roll the pastry out on a floured surface. Wrap it up around the sides and over the top of the cheese, pressing the edges together to seal it completely. Trim the excess and keep it for decoration.
Turn the parcel over so the gathered pastry is underneath and set it on a greased baking sheet. It can be refrigerated at this point for up to 2 days; bring it back to room temperature before baking.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Beat the egg with the water and brush it over the top and sides of the pastry. Add any decorations from the leftover pastry and brush those too.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, until the pastry is deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes and serve with more jam.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0cc.description: Flourless banana and egg pancakes topped with pecans and raspberries.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0f5.description: Soft buns made from bread mix, filled with sticky soy, honey and ginger bacon and baked until golden.
instructions: Mix the sugar into the bread mix in a large bowl, then add water as instructed on the pack. Bring the dough together with a wooden spoon, then knead on a lightly floured surface for 5 minutes until smooth. Put it in a large bowl, cover with oiled cling film and leave in a warm place until doubled in size.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan and fry the bacon until crisp, about 5 minutes. Add the ginger and garlic and fry for 1 minute until soft, then add the soy, honey and tomato purée and stir well. The filling can be made up to 3 days ahead.
Turn out the dough, knead briefly and divide into 12 even balls. Flatten each with your hands and put a teaspoon of filling in the middle.
Draw the dough up and pinch it closed like a purse, then turn the bun over and sit it on a large baking sheet. Cover with oiled cling film and leave to rise for about 30 minutes until pillowy.
Heat the oven to 200°C/fan 180°C/gas 6. Brush the buns with egg and bake for 20 minutes until golden.
Serve warm with a dipping sauce. The buns can be frozen after the second rise for up to a month, or baked a day ahead and rewarmed.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0c6.description: A quick Chinese stir-fry of marinated sirloin and broccoli in an oyster-sauce glaze.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e131.description: Rice bowls topped with sweet soy beef, grated carrot, quick-pickled cucumber and sriracha mayo.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e163.description: Beef shin braised for three hours in red wine with bacon, shallots and mushrooms, served with a spiced celeriac mash.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e140.description: Filipino beef stew in a tomato and peanut sauce with peppers, potato and carrot.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0e3.description: Uruguayan baked empanadas: a lard pastry around a filling of seared steak, tomato, onion and boiled egg.
instructions: Make the dough: put the lard, warm water and salt in a large bowl and stir. Add the flour and oregano and knead for 5 minutes by hand or in a machine. Cover and rest for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.

Make the filling: put the tomatoes in boiling water for about 30 seconds, cool them in cold water, then peel and dice. Crush the garlic and dice the onions. Simmer the garlic and onions in a little olive oil until translucent.

Take out the onions and garlic and brown the meat on all sides over a high heat. Season with the herbs and spices, return the onions and garlic, add the tomatoes and simmer for a few minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Boil the eggs, dice them and mix them into the meat. The filling can be made the night before and chilled.

Cut the dough in half and roll one half out thinly on a floured surface. Cut out 12–15cm circles. Put 2–4 teaspoons of filling on each, wet the edges, fold into half-moons and seal with a fork. Repeat until the dough and filling are used up.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Brush the empanadas with egg wash and bake about 8 at a time on a lined baking sheet for about 25 minutes, until golden. Serve warm with chimichurri.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e153.description: Vietnamese beef noodle soup: a charred onion, ginger and star-anise broth poured over rice noodles and thinly sliced raw sirloin.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0cd.description: Roast beef and potatoes with boiled vegetables and Yorkshire puddings.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e133.description: Purple pancakes blended with cooked beetroot, served with a quick berry compote and yogurt.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0c3.description: A simple beetroot, potato and cannellini bean soup finished with dill.

Add the drained beans and cook for 5 minutes more. Season and serve garnished with dill.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e105.description: Filipino beef steak marinated in soy and lemon, braised until tender and topped with fried onions.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0eb.description: Beef and chorizo chilli with ancho chillies and borlotti beans, braised low and slow for three hours.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e173.description: Cabbage leaves rolled around rice, chestnuts and cranberries and baked in a sweet-sharp stock.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e146.description: An Indian street-food breakfast: bread pressed into a thin omelette, toasted and folded into a sandwich.
instructions: Beat the eggs with the salt in a shallow bowl.
Heat a little butter or oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and pour in the eggs, tilting the pan to spread them thinly.
Before the top sets, lay the two slices of bread side by side on the egg and press lightly so they stick.
When the underside is golden, flip the whole thing so the bread toasts, about a minute.
Fold the egg edges over the bread, fold in half into a sandwich and serve hot.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e115.description: Colombian breaded steak: thin pounded beef marinated in aliños sauce, crumbed and pan-fried.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e10d.title: Breadfruit in Butter Sauce
6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e10d.description: Jamaican boiled breadfruit served under a buttery tomato, onion and garlic sauce.
instructions: Cut the breadfruit, remove the seeds from the core and peel. Boil in salted water with the half onion and the olive oil over a high heat until tender, then drain and leave to cool.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a frying pan and lightly brown the onions, cut into rings. Add the garlic, tomatoes, parsley, lime juice, salt and pepper and sauté for a couple of minutes.
Add the water, bring to the boil and simmer for 5–10 minutes. Season with red pepper sauce.
Slice the breadfruit into a serving dish, pour the butter sauce over and garnish with chopped parsley.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0be.description: A savoury cream cheese and parmesan tart topped with tomatoes in a warm honey-vinegar dressing.

Spoon the tomatoes onto the tart, leaving most of the liquid behind, and finish with basil leaves.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e0c0.description: A soft white bread from Dominica, enriched with shortening and kneaded twice for a close crumb.
instructions: Mix the flour, sugar, salt and instant yeast in a large bowl with a wooden spoon. (If you have active dry yeast instead, first dissolve it with the sugar in the warm water at 115–120°F, stir in a pinch of salt and ½ lb of the flour, and leave somewhere warm for about an hour until foamy, then add it to the rest of the flour.)
Add the shortening or lard and mix it in thoroughly with your hands.
Add the warm water and mix to a stiff dough, adding a little more flour if it sticks.
Turn the dough onto a floured board and knead for 8–10 minutes.
Shape into a large round, cover and leave to rest for 45 minutes.
Knead again on a lightly floured surface; this second kneading matters most. Shape into loaves or rolls and set them on a baking sheet or in tins.
Leave to rest for 25 minutes. Meanwhile heat the oven to 375°F.
Bake until golden brown and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath.

6aa77cd4b13a3d3c6ab2e12b.description: Rustic Caribbean coconut rock cakes spiced with cinnamon, nutmeg and lime zest.

instructions: Mix the yeast with the warm water and leave for a few minutes. Sift the flour with the salt into a large bowl, then gradually add the yeast water and mix with your hand until the dough forms a ball. (A bread machine's dough cycle also works.)

Punch the dough down and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Stretch it into an oblong, then roll it about ½ inch thick. Transfer to a greased baking sheet and leave for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Cut crosshatches into the top of the dough, about four in each direction. Brush with the egg yolk beaten with a little water and sprinkle with poppy seeds.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, until golden on top.
